about: ✎ PENCIL. Hand-maintained, read by queries.ts. Each query below is what the exhaustive enumeration (research/conformance/) observed on the date given: it names the finding and what would settle it, or, once `triaged` is true, its class and a one-line note, taking no other position on the cause. If findings/triage.json becomes the one home for a finding's status, fold `triaged` and `finding` into it.

defaults.$note: The expectation for any query not named below: the P0.3 properties as stated in docs/research-programme.md, not observations.

CONFLICT/26b-id+30a.would_settle: Retired: colregs@0.2.2 answered this by changing 26b-id's relation to 30a from rel:excludes to rel:overrides. excludingPairs() no longer pairs them, so buildQueries() no longer produces this id at all -- kept here only as the historical record of the finding this settled, not as a live query.

CONFLICT/26c-id+30a.would_settle: Retired, same ruling as CONFLICT/26b-id+30a: 26c-id's relation to 30a changed from rel:excludes to rel:overrides in colregs@0.2.2.

NO-OBLIGATION/any.would_settle: Settled: Rule 3(i) rules a vessel made fast to the shore out of Rule 30 entirely, prescribing no lights at all. run.ts EXPECTED_EMPTY_POSITIONS and its README record this ruling for position:moored; findings/triage.json no longer carries a separate entry for it.

NO-OBLIGATION/not-moored.observed_by: npm run conformance, check consistency-no-obligation, position breakdown: every zero-obligation record was position:moored
NO-OBLIGATION/not-moored.note: Every record not position:moored satisfies some encoded display entry's `when`; the one empty record is the moored one (Rule 3(i), NO-OBLIGATION/any). A claim about total records only (encode.ts header, point 2).

CONFLICT/rule:25b+rule:25c.note: rule:25b and rule:25c are both modality:may, and encode.ts defines |shall:<id>| false for any entry not modality:shall, so they cannot both resolve to shall.
